clue.text: Top Union appointment protects millions

indicators.note: to protect is to surround and shelter, so the job word wraps around the letter

parts.note: a post is a job or appointment
M is the abbreviation for million(s)

explanation.surface: A senior trade-union job is shielded by millions of pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Uppermost and upmost are adjectives for whatever sits highest, the same sense as top.

clue.text: Angry diatribe, right after being abandoned by international merchant

indicators.note: the right letter comes after the shortened diatribe word
the diatribe word is left behind by the international letter, which drops out of it

parts.note: a tirade is a long angry speech

explanation.surface: A furious rant, delivered right after an overseas merchant walked out.
explanation.definitionFit: A trader buys and sells goods for a living, which is what a merchant does.

clue.text: Speak tartly: "Those are identical!"

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to speak sharply or irritably
second meaning: the cry in the card game where players call out on matching cards

explanation.walkthrough: Snap is a children's card game in which you shout the name when two matching cards turn up.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to make a curt, irritable remark, and the exclamation is the call in the matching-cards game.

clue.text: Painting of fresh cod with tails removed

indicators.note: each of the two words loses its tail, meaning its final letter is cut off

explanation.surface: A still-life picture of a freshly caught cod, with the fish tails cut off.
explanation.definitionFit: A fresco is a mural made by painting onto wet plaster, so it is a kind of painting.

clue.text: Worried a contemptible chap and a delinquent youth

parts.note: git is British slang for a contemptible man
a Ted, short for Teddy boy, was a 1950s British youth associated with rowdy behaviour

explanation.surface: Someone is worried about a nasty man and a young troublemaker.
explanation.definitionFit: Agitated means anxious or troubled, a synonym for worried.

clue.text: Capturing my radical final gamble failing, ultimately

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like 'my!'
R is an abbreviation for radical, as in chemistry
going all in is staking everything on one last bet

indicators.note: ultimately points to the very end of the word failing, its last letter

explanation.surface: A last reckless bet fails and someone exclaims about it.
explanation.walkthrough: COR is a British exclamation ('Cor!') equal to 'My!'. In poker, going all-in means betting all your chips, so it is the last bet you can make.
explanation.definitionFit: To corral animals or people is to herd them into an enclosure, a kind of capturing.

clue.text: Make meals with BSE, unfortunately

indicators.note: things going unfortunately go wrong, so the letters end up in a different order

explanation.surface: Cooking dinners using beef infected with mad cow disease would be a bad idea.
explanation.walkthrough: BSE (bovine spongiform encephalopathy) is mad cow disease, a scare in British beef in the 1990s.
explanation.definitionFit: To assemble something is to put its parts together, that is to construct or make it.

clue.text: Beckham to tolerate playing occasionally

parts.note: to brook something is to tolerate it

indicators.note: occasionally means only now and then, so only every other letter of playing is used

explanation.surface: David Beckham puts up with playing football only now and then.
explanation.definitionFit: Brooklyn Beckham is the eldest son of the footballer David Beckham, so the name is an example.

clue.text: Run to seduce retiring husband?

indicators.note: to means added to, so the run letter is attached at the end
retiring means drawing back, so the word for seduce is read backwards

parts.note: to entrap someone is to lure or seduce them into a trap
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Someone runs off to seduce a shy husband.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as an example: a husband is one kind of partner.
explanation.definitionFit: A partner is a spouse or companion, and a husband is one instance of that.

clue.text: On the radio, shopkeeper is more boorish

indicators.note: on the radio things are only heard, so the word is the one that sounds like the shopkeeper

parts.note: a grocer is a shopkeeper who sells food

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper interviewed on the radio comes across as rather rude.
explanation.definitionFit: Gross can mean coarse and vulgar, so its comparative matches more boorish.

clue.text: Do I use power to corrupt tragic hero?

indicators.note: corrupting something spoils and distorts its form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for power in physics

explanation.surface: An actor asks whether to abuse power while playing a tragic role.
explanation.definitionFit: Oedipus, the king in Sophocles' drama who unknowingly killed his father, is a classic Greek tragic protagonist.

clue.text: Overrode protestor about concealing weapon

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the concealed letters are read backwards
the two words conceal the answer within their letters across the gap

explanation.surface: Authorities overruled a demonstrator who was hiding a weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A torpedo is a self-propelled underwater missile, a naval weapon.

clue.text: Exhaustively discuss stuff no longer popular

parts.note: to stuff an opponent is to beat them heavily, to thrash them
out means out of fashion, no longer in

explanation.surface: People talk at length about old things that have gone out of fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: To thrash out a problem is to argue it through thoroughly until it is settled.

clue.text: Avoided dealing with port covered by fish

indicators.note: in a down entry the port sits beneath, so is covered by, the fish

parts.note: skate is a flat fish
Dover is a ferry port on England's south coast

explanation.surface: A port town is buried under a heap of fish.
explanation.definitionFit: To skate over a matter is to idiomatically pass over it lightly, avoiding proper treatment.

clue.text: Name of beautiful Italian cycling

indicators.note: cycling means going round, so letters move from the front of the Italian word to the back

parts.note: bella is Italian for beautiful

explanation.surface: The name of a lovely Italian woman out on her bicycle.
explanation.definitionFit: A label is a tag giving something's identification, so as a verb or noun it means name.

clue.text: Sugar, perhaps stored in hardened wax?

indicators.note: stored in means placed inside, so the name goes within the hardened word

parts.note: set means hardened, as of glue or concrete
Alan is the first name of Alan Sugar, the British businessman of TV's The Apprentice; perhaps marks him as an example of an Alan

explanation.surface: Sugar might be kept inside a block of solidified wax.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sugar' looks like the sweetener but is Lord Alan Sugar, a well-known British entrepreneur. The question mark shows wax is only one example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sealing wax is used to close envelopes, so wax is one example of a substance that seals.

clue.text: I know not of cashmere pants

indicators.note: pants is British slang for rubbish or poor, so the letters of cashmere come out badly ordered

explanation.surface: Someone professes ignorance about cashmere trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pants' looks like trousers, but in British slang it means rubbish, which signals the letters are jumbled.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Search me' is an idiom said when you have no idea of the answer.

clue.text: Where you might buy Hoover for water?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the Hoover Dam would be bought at a sale of dams
second meaning: an old jocular name for drinking water

explanation.walkthrough: 'Hoover' looks like the vacuum cleaner, but it is the Hoover Dam on the Colorado River; split the letters differently and you get a dam sale.
explanation.definitionFit: Adam's ale is a humorous phrase for plain water, the only drink the first man had.

clue.text: Review of officials following wild rant leads to relocation

indicators.note: the reversed officials word follows the rearranged rant
wild means out of control, so the letters of rant are thrown into a new order
a review looks back over something, so the officials word is read backwards

parts.note: refs, short for referees, are match officials

explanation.surface: After a furious outburst, the referees are reassessed and moved elsewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: A transfer is a move from one place to another, a synonym for relocation.

clue.text: Doctor beginning to inspect fissure in cinema

indicators.note: the beginning of inspect is its first letter

parts.note: a vein is a crack in rock filled with mineral deposits

explanation.surface: A doctor starts examining a crack in a picture house.
explanation.definitionFit: A drive-in is an open-air cinema where films are watched from parked cars.

clue.text: Native American husband leaves quickly

indicators.note: leaves means departs, so the husband letter goes out of the people's name

parts.note: the Apache are a Native American people

explanation.surface: A Native American man's husband walks out in a hurry.
explanation.definitionFit: Apace is an adverb meaning swiftly, at a fast speed.

clue.text: Every one cooked goat with rare reptile

parts.note: every can mean all
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: cooked suggests something prepared and altered, so the letters of goat are reworked

explanation.surface: Everyone ate roast goat served with rare reptile meat.
explanation.definitionFit: An alligator is a large American crocodilian, a type of reptile.

clue.text: Inauguration of large corporation originally cancelled

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing sizes

indicators.note: originally refers to the first letter, which is cancelled from the belly word

parts.note: corporation is an old jocular word for a pot belly, a paunch

explanation.surface: The launch of a big company is called off at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corporation' looks like a company, but it is an old British jokey term for a large belly.
explanation.definitionFit: A launch is the formal start or unveiling of something, an inauguration.

clue.text: Monitored unusual gadget

indicators.note: unusual means out of the ordinary, so the letters of gadget take an uncommon order

explanation.surface: An odd piece of kit was kept under surveillance.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal or offender who is tagged carries an electronic tracker so their movements can be tracked.

clue.text: Crows over legendary horse

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the collective noun is read backwards

parts.note: a group of crows is called a murder

explanation.surface: Birds fly over a famous racehorse.
explanation.walkthrough: A murder of crows is the collective noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Red Rum was the racehorse who won Britain's Grand National steeplechase three times in the 1970s, a famous champion.

clue.text: Swear about male's habits

indicators.note: about means around, so the swearing word goes round the male

parts.note: to cuss is to swear
a tom is a male cat, and the 's means is, a link

explanation.surface: Swearing is one of this man's bad habits.
explanation.definitionFit: Customs are established practices or traditions, the same as habits.

clue.text: Free guidance at work I ignored

indicators.note: letters at work are busy being reshaped, so guidance is rearranged
ignored means left out, so the letter I is not used in the rearrangement

explanation.surface: Free advice given in the office, which I took no notice of.
explanation.definitionFit: An uncaged animal has been released from its cage, so it is set free.

clue.text: Tea-time conversation

parts.note: cha is a British informal word for tea

explanation.surface: People talking over afternoon tea.
explanation.definitionFit: A chat is an informal talk, so it is a conversation.

clue.text: French playwright to a greater extent describes story

indicators.note: to describe a shape is to draw around it, so more surrounds the lie

parts.note: more means to a greater extent
a story can be an untruth, a lie

explanation.surface: A French dramatist tells a story at greater length.
explanation.definitionFit: Molière was the seventeenth-century comic dramatist of Tartuffe, France's best-known writer for the stage.

clue.text: Man with tetanus regularly removed hat

parts.note: a chap is a man

indicators.note: every other letter of tetanus is removed at regular intervals, leaving the rest

explanation.surface: A man suffering from lockjaw took his hat off.
explanation.definitionFit: Chapeau is the French word for hat, used in English for a headpiece.
